newsitem.title: UK: UK construction output growth set to pick up.
newsitem.headline: UK construction output growth set to pick up.

text.p: Total construction output in Britain is expected to rise by two percent in 1997 and by a further three percent in 1998, the Building Material Producers group said on Monday.
The group predicted in a three-year outlook that output growth would slow down to two percent in 1999. The BMP said the upturn would be fuelled by growth in the housing and commercial sectors.
In 1996, total output was up 0.9 percent.

The BMP said the seven percent rise over the coming years would be assisted by the revitalised private housing market, a flurry of new office developments and entertainment projects which embraced Millennium and National Lottery deals.
The BMP said the entertainment projects would see the fastest growth this year, with double digit increases expected.
BMP said 160,000 new private homes would be started this year, a rise of 10 percent on 1996. Output in the commercial sector would grow by eight percent this year and next, the group said.

Charles Novotny, chairman of BMP's forecast panel, said the growth predicted in its survey would have been even higher if there hadn't been a seven percent cut in government spending on public infrastructure and buildings.
